# clippy-gate-baseline — packages NOT yet covered by the deny-tier clippy gate.
#
# Same shape, and the same contract, as runtime-install-baseline.txt: an entry
# here is TRACKED DEBT, not an exemption. The list may only SHRINK. Nothing is
# added to it — a new crate is gated from birth by adding it to the
# `clippy-gate` alias in .cargo/config.toml, never by landing it here.
#
# WHY THESE ARE HERE, stated once and honestly: they are not known-dirty, they
# are UNMEASURED. Establishing that a package is deny-tier clean requires
# compiling it, and this baseline was produced on a workstation that was at 97%
# disk with other builds running, under an explicit instruction not to build the
# workspace. So the gate covers exactly what was compiled and observed green
# (`cargo clippy -p sui-eval`, which pulls in seven workspace siblings and
# therefore lints all eight), and every package that was not compiled is listed
# below rather than assumed clean. An unmeasured package silently included in
# the gate is how a gate ends up red on arrival.
#
# Graduating one is a small, bounded task: run `cargo clippy -p <name>`, and if
# it exits 0, move the name into the alias and delete its line here. The
# per-line note records what is actually known about each.
#
# ── denominator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gated:     8   (the `clippy-gate` alias in .cargo/config.toml)
# ungated:  23   (the entries below)
# total:    31   (30 `members` in Cargo.toml + the root package pleme-io-sui)
#
# 8 + 23 = 31. If that sum stops holding, one of the three files disagrees with
# the workspace and the gate is examining something other than what it claims.
# The workflow floors the gated count before it runs clippy; the ungated count
# is carried here so the COVERAGE FRACTION is reviewable rather than implied.
# Coverage today is 8/31 = 25.8% of packages. Stating that plainly is the point
# — a gate whose scope is unstated reads as total.

# ── ungated packages (measurement missing) ───────────────────────────────
pleme-io-sui                        # root package + the `sui` binary; largest build
canteiro-types
sui-bigorna
sui-build
sui-cache
sui-cache-eval
sui-castore
sui-daemon
sui-daemon-client
sui-daemon-frame
sui-daemon-graph
sui-dockerfile-node-cache-daemon
sui-dockerfile-prewarmer
sui-dockerfile-verify
sui-dockerfile-wrapper
sui-fmt
sui-ir
sui-lsp
sui-nix-wrap
sui-orchestrate
sui-protocol
sui-registry
sui-supercacheci

# ── target-kind debt: --all-targets is NOT gated ─────────────────────────
# This one IS measured, and it is the reason the alias stops at the default
# targets (lib + bins) instead of adding `--all-targets`.
#
# `cargo clippy -p sui-eval --lib --tests` exits 101 with 14 errors, all
# `clippy::approx_constant` (deny-by-default), all of the shape:
#
#   sui-eval/src/convert.rs:153
#     assert_eq!(string_keyed_to_eval(&StringKeyedValue::Float(3.14)),
#                Value::Float(3.14));
#     error: approximate value of `f{32, 64}::consts::PI` found
#
# These are arbitrary float fixtures, not an intended PI, so the lint is
# correct about the literal and wrong about the intent. Graduating this means
# choosing a fixture value clippy does not recognise (or a scoped
# `#[allow(clippy::approx_constant)]` on the test modules, which is weaker) and
# then adding `--all-targets` to the alias. It is deliberately NOT bundled into
# the change that introduced this gate: it edits test fixtures, and the run
# that would prove those tests still pass is a heavier build than the gate.
#
# Until then, test/bench/example targets are unlinted at deny tier for every
# package, gated or not.
--all-targets                       # blocked: 14 approx_constant in sui-eval tests
